vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pay-bills
Version: 0.0.2

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its handling of sensitive data. It stores session tokens and device IDs in plain-text files (`.session_token`, `.device_id`) within the skill's directory, as seen in `session-token.js` and `generate-device-id.js`. While this local persistence is necessary for the skill's stated purpose of managing user sessions and device identification for the `lodu.bleon.net` API, it represents a vulnerability. If the skill's local environment is compromised, these sensitive credentials could be exposed, allowing unauthorized access to the user's account on the external service. The `SKILL.md` instructions are transparent about this behavior and do not exhibit malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (buying airtime/data via the Bleon API); nothing in the files indicates hidden exfiltration or unrelated privileges, though the SKILL.md expects Node.js even though the declared requirements list no binaries and the source has no public homepage.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (buy data/airtime for Nigerian numbers) matches the included SKILL.md and the three helper Node.js scripts (order id, device id, session token). Minor inconsistency: SKILL.md instructs to run the scripts with node, but the skill metadata lists no required binaries — Node.js is effectively required but not declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to authenticating with and calling endpoints at the documented base URL, using local device/session files and generated trx_ids. The SKILL.md does not instruct reading unrelated system files, environment variables, or sending data to other endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + small JS helper files). The code is small, local, and there are no downloads or external install steps that would fetch arbitrary code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. It persists only two local files (.session_token and .device_id) in the skill directory to manage auth and device identity — this is proportional to the described auth flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation. The scripts persist tokens/IDs only to files in their own directory and do not modify other skills or system configs. No elevated privileges are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and implements local helper scripts for the documented API. Before installing: ensure Node.js is available (SKILL.md requires running node but the registry metadata omits that), verify you trust the remote API host (https://lodu.bleon.net) since the package has no homepage and an unknown source, and be aware the skill will create .session_token and .device_id files in the skill directory — keep that directory private or clear the token with the included clear command when you log out. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a homepage or official repo and confirm the API endpoint is legitimate.
